key_insight: The paper shows that several subquadratic sequence models can replace standard Transformers for long-context tasks with much lower compute, but their effectiveness depends on the design choice and the task. It compares xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet to identify which architectures work best for complex dependencies such as code modeling.
problem_solved: Transformers are powerful but expensive because self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length. This paper addresses the need for faster, more scalable sequence models that still handle long-range dependencies well.
method: Compare three leading subquadratic architectures: xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet.
Evaluate them on challenging dependency-heavy settings including code-model pre-training and distillation from large language models.
Analyze performance trade-offs to determine which architectural principles are most effective for scalable sequence modeling.
impact: For practitioners, this helps identify practical alternatives to Transformers when memory and compute are bottlenecks. The results can guide model selection for long-context applications like code generation, distillation, and efficient pretraining.

paper_title: On Subquadratic Architectures: From Applications to Principles
paper_authors: Anamaria-Roberta Hartl, Levente Zólyomi, David Stap, Pieter-Jan Hoedt, Niklas Schmidinger
